record.title: Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy AI
record.short_title: EU Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy AI
record.issuing_body: European Commission, High-Level Expert Group on Artificial Intelligence (AI HLEG)
record.summary: Guidelines by the Commission's independent High-Level Expert Group on AI, setting out a framework for trustworthy AI that is lawful, ethical and robust. They give seven key requirements: human agency and oversight, technical robustness and safety, privacy and data governance, transparency, diversity and non-discrimination, societal and environmental well-being, and accountability, with an assessment list to apply them.
record.notes: Written by the AI HLEG, whose members support the overall framework but not necessarily every statement; the views do not represent an official Commission position. A draft of 18 December 2018 drew more than 500 comments. The assessment list was piloted from 26 June to 1 December 2019 and presented as the final Assessment List for Trustworthy AI (ALTAI), made public on 17 July 2020. The Commission page offers the text in 23 EU languages.
record.scope_note: A report by an expert group that the European Commission convened and publishes, not an act of the Commission itself; included as the EU's foundational trustworthy-AI guidance.

verification.note: Stored copies: the Commission page, its printable PDF and the English PDF of the Guidelines (stored as an extra source), plus the ALTAI PDF. Title, date and non-binding character confirmed from the English PDF and page.
